meta.beschreibung: Portable, water-saving shower and washing systems that work without electricity and without plumbing. For van life, camping, travel and places with no running water.
start.hero.text: Shower, wash, rinse — with a fraction of the water, no power, no plumbing. Folded up, the whole thing fits in a jacket pocket.
start.problem.text: In the van, at a festival, in a mountain hut, after a long day: the moment you want to wash arrives reliably — the tap does not. The usual answers are heavy, need power, or empty half a canister in five minutes.
start.problem.punkt1.text: Everything runs on gravity and hand pressure. No pump, no battery, nothing that can run flat.
start.problem.punkt2.text: A bottle, a canister, a bucket — whatever is there will do. No hose, no installation.
start.problem.punkt3.text: The fine jet puts the water exactly where it belongs. One litre becomes a full wash.
start.produkte.text: Seven sets, one principle — depending on whether you want to shower, rinse, or freshen up on the move.

start.einsatz.reise.text: Between a night bus and a hostel with no shower, one litre is enough to feel human again.

1plus1.untertitel: The principle is simple. Keeping it honest is the actual work.
1plus1.wie.schritt1.text: Normally, at the listed price. The donated unit is part of our calculation, not a surcharge on top.
1plus1.wie.schritt2.text: When ordering, you decide which organisation receives the donated set.
1plus1.wie.schritt3.text: Once enough sets have accumulated, a delivery goes out — with photo, date and quantity on the transparency page.
1plus1.kritik.text: The 1+1 model has a reputation to lose. TOMS Shoes made it famous and was criticised for years: donated goods can undercut local traders, they solve no structural problem, and they mostly serve the buyer's good conscience. That criticism is fair. So here is what we do differently — and what we do not claim.
1plus1.faq.1.antwort: Our recipients are in Germany and Europe, not in countries with functioning local markets for these products. And the people who receive a set would not be a local trader's customers — there is simply no offer for them. We are not taking a sale away from anyone.
1plus1.faq.2.frage: Does this solve a structural problem?
1plus1.faq.2.antwort: No. A shower set replaces no flat, no social policy and no water infrastructure. It makes one specific day more bearable. We claim no more than that — and no less.
1plus1.faq.3.frage: Who decides who receives a set?
1plus1.faq.3.antwort: The organisations, not us. They employ people who know their clients. We deliver to the organisation and stay out of the distribution.
1plus1.faq.4.frage: Do I get a donation receipt?
1plus1.faq.4.antwort: No. You buy a product, you do not donate — we make the donation. We cannot issue a tax receipt because we are not a registered charity. If you need one, donate directly to the organisation; we link to them on every project page.
1plus1.faq.5.frage: How do I know the sets arrive?
1plus1.faq.5.antwort: The transparency page lists every delivery with date, quantity, recipient and proof. The counter on the home page reflects only these confirmed deliveries — never the orders. If a number is shown there, the goods have arrived.
1plus1.faq.6.frage: Why does the counter show zero?
1plus1.faq.6.antwort: Because no partner agreement has been signed yet. We could extrapolate a number from orders — that would be a promise with nothing behind it. Once the first delivery goes out, this changes.
1plus1.stand.text: The model is prepared but not yet active. We are talking to social organisations; as soon as an agreement is in place, we will name the organisation, the quantity and the timeframe here. Until then: no donation promise, and no advertising with one.

ueber.geschichte.titel: It started at a kitchen table in Warsaw
ueber.geschichte.p1: The idea for a washing device that gets by on very little water came about in 2014. A year later Zdzisław Iwanejko built the first Handy Shower prototypes together with his children Zuzanna and Alexander — by hand, to try it out.
ueber.geschichte.p2: In 2017 it became a company based in Warsaw: first under the name HandyShower, today WaSH Innovation. The underlying principle has stayed the same and is patented in several countries — one device that is shower, tap and bidet in one, working without electricity and without plumbing.
ueber.geschichte.p3: The ambition behind it goes beyond camping: basic hygiene should also be possible where fixed installations are missing, unreliable or destroyed — after disasters, in crisis regions, in care work.
ueber.vertrieb.titel: We bring the devices to Germany
ueber.vertrieb.text: WashInnovation.de is an independent distribution partner of WaSH Innovation. We did not invent the products — we make sure you can get them here, get advice in German, and have someone who writes back.
ueber.vertrieb.text2: The 1+1 model is not a requirement from the manufacturer but our own initiative. How far it has come and what is still missing is stated openly on the page about the model.

wasser.untertitel: Why one litre matters — sourced, not asserted.
wasser.welt.text: These figures come from the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme and from the UN World Water Development Report. Each one carries its source and date so it stays verifiable.
wasser.nutzung.text: Of the fresh water withdrawn worldwide, households take the smallest share. Looking at your own shower therefore does not explain the global picture — but it is the part you actually control.
wasser.nutzung.rundung: The shares are rounded and come from different survey years, which is why they add up to slightly more than one hundred per cent. The bars show the proportions, not an exact split.
wasser.deutschland.text: Here water is reliably there, in good quality, around the clock. That is good fortune, not guilt. The interesting question is what we use it for — and how far the same amount can go when it is used deliberately.
wasser.bogen.titel: What this has to do with these products
wasser.bogen.text1: The largest single item in a German household is personal hygiene: around 43.5 litres a day. A WaSH Innovation shower set manages a full wash with roughly one litre, because the fine spray puts the water where it is needed instead of letting it run past the body.
wasser.bogen.text2: The same principle that saves the tank in a van makes these sets useful wherever water has to be carried. That is exactly what the 1+1 model aims at: every set sold should bring a donated one with it.

wasser.quellen.hinweis: The figures are taken from a compiled report, not from our own analysis of the primary sources. Before using them in press work or campaigns, check them against the then-current editions of the JMP, the UN World Water Development Report and Destatis.
